title: Project Ledger
summary: The task ledger for this project. Epic PR-E01 is an example to read and then replace with your own.

waves.1: Foundations: the first working slice and the decisions it needs

gates.ledger: python Docs/Ledger/ledger.py check. Run python Docs/Ledger/ledger.py selftest as well whenever ledger.py changes.

conventions.ids: PR-Enn is an epic, PR-Enn.mm a task, PR-Dnn a decision. Stable; never renumbered or reused.
conventions.wave: The execution order. `next` shows the lowest wave with unfinished work. A task filed during later work takes the wave its work belongs to, not the wave being worked when it was filed.
conventions.files: The files a task may edit. An entry ending in / allows everything under it. A commit naming the task that touches anything else is refused, unless it is given --reason: then the paths are added to the task's files and recorded in its filesAdded with the reason and the date.
conventions.acceptance: check: what to run or read. expect: what passing shows. Every check must be able to fail.
conventions.status: planned | in-progress | blocked | done | withdrawn. A status is a claim; read the tree.
conventions.evidence: Required for done. Label it ran-it, read-in-the-code or read-in-a-document, and say what was observed, not what was concluded.
conventions.landed: The commit that closed a done task, stamped by ledger.py commit.
conventions.decisions: The owner's calls. A task that depends on an open decision cannot start. `next` asks one at a time. An open decision carries options (2 to 4, each a label and a detail, one recommended) so the owner can answer it on the ledger website; the answer waits in Saved/Ledger/answers.json until a session runs `apply`, and `next` prints waiting answers first.
conventions.commits: Ledger work commits only through python Docs/Ledger/ledger.py commit. Its subject starts with a task or epic id, or it names a role (Owner, Repair, Checkpoint, Ledger) and a reason.
conventions.outsideCommits: A commit made outside the tool that touched an in-progress task's files is RECORDED here with a reason, never excused by moving auditFrom.
conventions.auditFrom: Move only to a commit inside the window, after a green audit at the old mark, and say so in the commit.
conventions.ledgerFiles: The ledger is Docs/Ledger/meta.json plus one Docs/Ledger/epics/PR-Enn.json per epic, holding the epic, its tasks and the decisions filed under it. Change it through ledger.py (start, done, block, note, add-task, add-decision, decide, apply), which writes only the files that changed and refuses to overwrite a file another session changed after it read it. See Docs/Ledger/README.md.
conventions.owner: One name from meta.json 'departments', or the project owner. A task owned by a department other than the hub is a department subtask and carries 'kind'. The owner's part of another owner's task is its needs<Owner> field, in words.
conventions.kind: review, measure or produce: a department subtask. The hub dispatches it (ledger.py dispatch prints the department agent's prompt); the agent starts it with --by, records findings and hands it in with submit; only the hub's confirm, by a different --by, marks it done.
conventions.findings: Recorded on the subtask by the agent; the hub routes every finding to a task, or rejects it with a reason, before it confirms. blocker: data loss, corruption, a security hole or a crash on the priority path; its fixing task goes on the critical path now. hardening: everything else; its fixing task goes in the wave its work belongs to. Every finding points at something checkable (a repo path with :line, a log, a commit id).

departments.name: Engineering
departments.does: The hub: the main Claude Code session. Builds, files tasks and decisions, starts the department agents, confirms their work and routes their findings.

departments.name: Code Review Department
departments.does: Reads landed code for correctness bugs, data loss, security holes and broken contracts (review).

departments.name: Game Design Department
departments.does: Example for a game project: reviews designs, plans and tuning for the loop, challenge, progression and fun (review).
